concepts.title: Ocean Floor Relief and Salinity of Ocean Water
concepts.definition: The ocean floor shows continental shelf, slope, deep sea plain and trenches, and ocean water averages about 3.5 per cent or 35 parts per thousand salinity, varying with evaporation, precipitation, river influx and circulation from about 32 to 37 ppt in the open sea.
concepts.key_idea: Salinity is highest in subtropical seas of strong evaporation and lowest near river mouths and polar seas of melting ice and heavy rain.

solution_steps.action: divide salt by water mass and scale to thousand
solution_steps.explain: Divide the dissolved salt mass by the sea water mass and multiply by 1000 to get the salinity in parts per thousand

concepts.title: Ocean Temperature and the Hydrological Cycle
concepts.definition: Ocean water temperature falls with latitude and depth, and the oceans drive the hydrological cycle by evaporating water that returns as precipitation, while the heat capacity of the sea moderates the earth's climate.
concepts.key_idea: The upper warm layer, the thermocline of rapid temperature fall and the deep cold layer structure the ocean vertically.

concepts.title: Ocean Resources and Their Importance
concepts.definition: Oceans provide food from fisheries, minerals like oil, natural gas and polymetallic nodules, energy from tides and waves, and the sea routes that carry most world trade, making ocean resources vital to the economy and future food security.
concepts.key_idea: The seabed beyond national jurisdiction is treated as the common heritage of mankind under the law of the sea.
